## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $n\ge1$, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold
completed tensor power with $H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$, let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
be the permutation unitaries and let
$P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, be the sector projections
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), with sector space
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq H^{\otimes n}.$$
For $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
be the operator of clause (a) below, and put
$$\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^n O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n}).$$
Identify $H^{\otimes n}$ with $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ by the
surjective linear isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) below, and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}$ be the partial trace of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clause (a) over the
second factor of that identification. Then:

(a) *slot operators*: for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and every
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is a unique $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
with $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes Ov_i\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$
for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$; it satisfies $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$ and
$(O^*)^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$; in particular $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$;

(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$; for $n=1$ the
empty product is $1\in\mathbb C$ and $J_1u=u\otimes1$;

(c) *permutation invariance*: $U_\pi\,\Sigma(O)\,U_\pi^*=\Sigma(O)$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$; consequently $\Sigma(O)$ preserves both sector spaces and commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$:
$$\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)};$$

(d) *trace law*: for every density operator $\rho$ on the sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]
clause (a)), let $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow H^{\otimes n}$ be
the isometric inclusion and define its zero extension
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; then
for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\,\operatorname{tr}(\gamma\,O)$,
where $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\bigl(J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}\bigr)\in\mathcal B(H)$;

(e) *the reduced operator is a density operator*: the operator $\gamma$ of
clause (d) is a density operator on $H$; it is independent of the choice of
slot in the sense that it equals the partial trace of $\widetilde\rho$ over
the other $n-1$ slots in the parenthesisation in which the retained slot is
the one the display names; for $n=1$, $\gamma=\rho$. If
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\{0\}$, there is no density operator of trace one on
that sector, so clauses (d)-(e) make no assertion about a sector preparation;

(f) *scope*: clauses (a)-(e) are exact operator identities on the
finite-dimensional labelled tensor powers; no physical system, particle
species, preparation or measurement is asserted, and the parameter $n$ is a
dimension count of the construction, not an observed particle number.

step_quotes.quote: 1.3 [The zero extension and its symmetry] With $j$ the inclusion of the sector, $\widetilde\rho=j\rho j^*$ restricts to $\rho$ on the sector and vanishes on its orthogonal complement. It is self-adjoint and positive because $\langle\widetilde\rho x,x\rangle=\langle\rho j^*x,j^*x\rangle\ge0$; adjoining an orthonormal basis of the complement to one of the sector gives $\operatorname{tr}\widetilde\rho=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, so it is a density operator by [F6]. Since $jj^*=P_\sigma^{(n)}$ and $U_\pi j=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)j$ by [F4], $\widetilde\rho=P_\sigma^{(n)}\widetilde\rho P_\sigma^{(n)}$ and $U_\pi\widetilde\rho U_\pi^*=\widetilde\rho$ for every $\pi$. A zero sector admits no trace-one endomorphism, so no $\rho$ exists in that case. [F4, F6, F7, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 1.3 [The zero extension and its symmetry] With $j$ the inclusion of the sector, $\widetilde\rho=j\rho j^*$ restricts to $\rho$ on the sector and vanishes on its orthogonal complement. It is self-adjoint and positive because $\langle\widetilde\rho x,x\rangle=\langle\rho j^*x,j^*x\rangle\ge0$; adjoining an orthonormal basis of the complement to one of the sector gives $\operatorname{tr}\widetilde\rho=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, so it is a density operator by [F6]. 3.1 [Reduction to one slot, the trace law and the reduced operator] By steps 1.3 and 2.1 and [F7], for $\pi(1)=i$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho O^{(i)})=\operatorname{tr}(U_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi A_1)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)$. Set $R_n:=J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}$, an endomorphism of $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$. Its partial trace $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}R_n$ is an endomorphism of $H$ by [F5]. Step 1.2 and [F5], [F7] give $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\Sigma(O))=n\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)=n\operatorname{tr}(R_n(O\otimes I))=n\operatorname{tr}(\gamma O)$, proving (d). step_quotes.quote: 2.1 [Slot operators and the permutation invariance of their sum] Fix $i$, choose $\pi\in S_n$ with $\pi(1)=i$ and set $O^{(i)}:=U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; [F9] and step 1.2 give $\|O^{(i)}\|=\|O\otimes I\|\le\|O\|$, and [F3], [F4] give $(O^{(i)})^*=U_\pi J_n^{-1}(O^*\otimes I)J_nU_\pi^*=(O^*)^{(i)}$, so $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$. On elementary tensors, [F4] gives $U_\pi^*(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi(n)}$; step 1.2 replaces the first factor by $Ov_{\pi(1)}=Ov_i$; and $U_\pi$ then moves that factor to slot $\pi(1)=i$, leaving every other factor in its original slot, so $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Ov_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$. If $\pi'$ is another permutation with $\pi'(1)=i$, then $\tau:=\pi^{-1}\pi'$ fixes $1$ and $U_\tau A_1U_\tau^*$ agrees with $A_1$ on elementary tensors by [F1], [F3], hence equals it by [F8]; thus $U_{\pi'}A_1U_{\pi'}^*=U_\pi U_\tau A_1U_\tau^*U_\pi^*=U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*$ and $O^{(i)}$ is well defined, with the displayed elementary-tensor action. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $\mathfrak h$ be a
two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and let $H:=T_{u_1,u_1}\varepsilon=\varepsilon\,T_{u_1,u_1}$ be the
self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$
be the partition sum, canonical operator and entropy of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause
(a), with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $w_i$ the eigenvalues of a density
operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(1,2)$, and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac1Z\bigl(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1}\bigr)$$
is a density operator on $\mathfrak h$ that is not the maximally mixed state
$\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$;

(b) the mean energy is the exact identity
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z}=\frac{\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1},\qquad 0<\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2};$$

(c) the entropy and free energy satisfy
$$s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\frac{\beta\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}=\log\bigl(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\bigr)+\frac{\beta\varepsilon\,e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}},\qquad 0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log 2,$$
and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are exact algebraic identities for the
declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters
$\varepsilon,\beta>0$; no temperature, thermodynamic, equilibrium or
measurement interpretation is asserted, and the parameter $\beta$ carries no
physical dimension in this lemma.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [Exponential comparison] Since $\beta\varepsilon>0$, strict increase in [F3] gives $\exp(\beta\varepsilon)>\exp(0)=1$, and [F3] gives $\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)=1/\exp(\beta\varepsilon)\in(0,1)$; consequently $1<Z=1+\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)<2$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 [The canonical operator] By [F1] with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $(v_1,v_2)=(u_0,u_1)$, $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1})\in\mathcal D$, so $\rho_\beta$ is a density operator; its two weights are $Z^{-1}$ and $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}Z^{-1}$, which are distinct because $\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)\ne1$ by step 1.1. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_N)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^N$,
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}\,(e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N})=\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}\Bigr)e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N};$$

(b) *occupation eigenvalues and spectrum*: for every $N$-element subset
$J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ the Slater vector $e_J^\wedge$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b) is an
eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of
$\mathfrak H_N^-$ and $\mathfrak H_N^+$ respectively, so the spectrum of
$H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of these eigenvalues (with multiplicities
given by the number of configurations producing them); for $\sigma=-$ and
$N>d$ the sector space is $\{0\}$ and the model has no sector states;

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: write
$$\mathcal C_N^\sigma:=\{\lambda\in W(N,d):\lambda_j\le1\ \text{for every }j\ \text{if }\sigma=-\},\qquad M_N^\sigma:=|\mathcal C_N^\sigma|=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma.$$
The configuration counts are $M_N^- =\binom dN$ and
$M_N^+ =\binom{N+d-1}{N}$. For every $\beta>0$,
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is finite. If $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$, then $\mathcal C_N^-=\varnothing$,
$Z_N(\beta)=0$, and there is no ground eigenvalue or trace-one density
operator on the zero sector; in particular no normalized Gibbs density can
be formed there. Otherwise $M_N^\sigma>0$ and $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$.
In this nonzero-sector case, let
$$E_0:=\min_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda,\qquad E_{\max}:=\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda.$$
Then the actual Boltzmann bounds are
$$M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le Z_N(\beta)\le M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_0}.$$
No nonnegativity hypothesis on the $\varepsilon_j$ is imposed. For
$\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$,
$$E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)},\qquad E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)},$$
and for $\sigma=+$,
$$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)},\qquad E_{\max}=N\varepsilon_{(d)}.$$
For every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in either nonzero sector,
$\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on the
eigenspace of $E_0$;

(d) *reading and stationarity*: on a nonzero sector the pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the
model's assigned energy observable; in a declared sector preparation $\rho$
its outcome law is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$,
and in the pure preparation of each sector basis vector of clause (b) this
law is the point mass at the displayed eigenvalue; each such vector is a
stationary state of the model evolution $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and
the energy law of every declared sector preparation is the law of the finite
spectral sum in the sector basis;

(e) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the finite-mode idealization, on
the declared $h$ and on $W=0$; it asserts nothing for interacting models, for
spatial realizations, for infinite mode families, about thermal states or
equilibration, and about any laboratory system.

step_quotes.quote: 2.1 [Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Partition sum and the zero sector] Normalize the symmetric vectors to $\widetilde m_\lambda:=m_\lambda/\|m_\lambda\|$; by [F3] these form an orthonormal eigenbasis, as do the Slater vectors in the fermionic sector. The trace is therefore $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$, with the configuration counts $M_N^-=\binom dN$ and $M_N^+=\binom{N+d-1}{N}$ from [F4]. ## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and

$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, integer $N\ge1$ with nonzero sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, and the slot
operators $O^{(i)}$, sum $\Sigma(O)$ and one-body reduced preparation
$\gamma_\rho$ of that definition. Let $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ be self-adjoint
with declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *the readout is an assigned observable*: the sector operator
$A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so the
pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a);

(b) *the mean law*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ the mean of
the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals
$$m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr);$$

(c) *product-type preparations*: if $u_1,\dots,u_N\in K$ are pairwise
orthonormal and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi:=S(u_1,\dots,u_N)$ the Slater
vector of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (a) for $\sigma=-$, or $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$
for $\sigma=+$ (both unit vectors of the sector), then
$\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$ and
$$m_\rho(A_O)=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle;$$

(d) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the adopted sector of P6, on the
declared finite-mode idealization and on the declared preparation; it asserts
no measured mean, no property of an individual labelled particle, no
separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

2.1 [The mean law] Let $\rho$ be a declared sector preparation with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ and let $A_O$ be the readout of step 1.1. the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals

separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

## Statement

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] together with the
state, probability, dynamics and preparation postulates P1, P2, P4, P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition: the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] has sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ of finite dimension $D\ge1$ with self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$, assigned temperature $T>0$, inverse temperature
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ and eigen-decomposition
$H_N^\sigma=\sum_{j=1}^DE_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ with orthonormal eigenbasis
$(v_1,\dots,v_D)$ and real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$. Write
$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,
$\rho_\beta:=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$, and let
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(a) *the canonical preparation*: $Z_N\in(0,\infty)$ is a finite sum,
$q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j=1$, and $\rho_\beta$ is a declared sector preparation of
the model with
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=\frac1{Z_N}\sum_{j=1}^DE_je^{-\beta E_j},\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z_N+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma);$$

(b) *free-energy minimum*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ one
has $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log Z_N$;

(c) *uniqueness*: equality $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$ holds if and only if
$\rho=\rho_\beta$; consequently the canonical preparation is the unique
minimiser of the free-energy functional over the declared sector
preparations, and $F(\rho_\beta)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$;

(d) *degenerate case*: if $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ for a real $c$, then
$Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$,
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=c-k_BT\log D$;

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [The canonical preparation and its data] By [F1], $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ is a finite sum with $0<Z_N<\infty$; since $D\ge1$ each term is positive, so $q_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N>0$ with $\sum_jq_j=1$. By [F1] the operator $\rho_\beta=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, hence a declared sector preparation of the model, and the two displayed identities are the clauses of [F1] together with the entropy definition. This proves (a). [F1, algebra]

2.1 [The free-energy difference for every mixed preparation] Let $\rho=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be as in [F2] and put $p_{ij}=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$, $r_i=\sum_jp_{ij}q_j$. Each $r_i>0$ and $\sum_ir_i=\sum_jq_j\sum_ip_{ij}=1$. Use the entropy convention $\eta(w)=w\log w$ for $w>0$ and $\eta(0)=0$ (the notation $0\log0=0$ does not define $\log0$). The trace pairing and the entropy definition give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)=\sum_{i,j}w_ip_{ij}E_j$ and $s(\rho)=-\sum_i\eta(w_i)$. ## Statement

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] together with the
state, probability, dynamics and preparation postulates P1, P2, P4, P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition: the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] has sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ of finite dimension $D\ge1$ with self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$, assigned temperature $T>0$, inverse temperature
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ and eigen-decomposition
$H_N^\sigma=\sum_{j=1}^DE_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ with orthonormal eigenbasis
$(v_1,\dots,v_D)$ and real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$. Write
$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,
$\rho_\beta:=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$, and let
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(a) *the canonical preparation*: $Z_N\in(0,\infty)$ is a finite sum,
$q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j=1$, and $\rho_\beta$ is a declared sector preparation of
the model with
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=\frac1{Z_N}\sum_{j=1}^DE_je^{-\beta E_j},\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z_N+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma);$$

(b) *free-energy minimum*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ one
has $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log Z_N$;

(c) *uniqueness*: equality $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$ holds if and only if
$\rho=\rho_\beta$; consequently the canonical preparation is the unique
minimiser of the free-energy functional over the declared sector
preparations, and $F(\rho_\beta)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$;

(d) *degenerate case*: if $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ for a real $c$, then
$Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$,
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=c-k_BT\log D$;

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

step_quotes.quote: 3.1 [Equality, strict zero-weight exclusion and degeneracies] If $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, the finite sum of nonnegative defects in step 2.1 vanishes. Hence $d(w_i,r_i)=0$ for every $i$; step 1.2 gives $w_i=r_i>0$, since $d(0,r_i)=r_i>0$ excludes every zero weight. Thus $w_i a_i=0$ forces $a_i=0$ for every row, and step 2.1 gives $q_j=r_i=w_i$ whenever $p_{ij}>0$. In the expansion of $u_i$ in the orthonormal basis $(v_j)$, the coefficients at all $q_j\ne w_i$ therefore vanish, so $\rho_\beta u_i=w_i u_i$. Conversely $\rho=\rho_\beta$ gives equality by [F1]. Together with step 2.1, this proves (c) with no full-rank assumption on the competing preparation. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

anchors.claim_quote:
## Statement

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the mode models
declared below, the state and probability postulates P1, P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]); assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Temperatures are assigned as in
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], so that
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Then:

(a) *single bosonic mode*: let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with
number operator $N$ and orthonormal number basis $(e_n)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]]), let
$\varepsilon>0$ and let the model declare the energy operator $H:=\varepsilon N$
on $F(\mathbb C)$; the model's canonical preparation at temperature $T$ is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, the
number readout $N$ is an assigned sharp observable with finite thermal mean
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}=\frac1{e^{\varepsilon/(k_BT)}-1},$$
and all moments $\langle N^k\rangle_\beta$, $k\ge1$, are finite;

(b) *single fermionic orbital and grand-canonical shift*: on
$\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^2$ with occupation operator $N_-$ and
$\varepsilon_1,\mu\in\mathbb R$, the model's canonical (grand-canonical)
preparation $F=Z^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}T_{u_k,u_k}$
has $Z=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$, $\operatorname{tr}F=1$, and occupation mean
$$\langle N_-\rangle=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1};$$
the same formula is the model's thermal mean when $\mu=0$ and
$\varepsilon_1>0$;

(c) *countably many independent modes*: let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$
and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, and let the model declare the free-mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ (one mode case of clause (a)) with the product reading of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]; then the
bosonic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$ and $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$, and
the fermionic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$; in the finite cases the products
equal $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})^{-1}$ and
$\prod_j(1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})$ respectively;

(d) *dilute remainders*: for $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$ the model's
occupation means satisfy the exact identities
$$\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q}\quad(\text{bosonic},\ 0<q<1),\qquad \frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q}\quad(\text{fermionic},\ q>0),$$
so both differ from $q$ by at most $q^2/(1-q)$ and $q^2/(1+q)$
respectively;

(e) *scope*: clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared
mode models together with the adopted ensemble assignment; they assert no
thermodynamic limit, no continuum of radiation modes, no Bose-Einstein
condensation, no measured occupation number, and no thermalisation of a
sample. All numerical equalities are exact identities of the declared
finite-mode (or product) models at the assigned temperature.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [The single bosonic mode] Apply [F1] with $\omega=\varepsilon$: $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical preparation of the declared energy operator $\varepsilon N$, the number readout $N$ is self-adjoint with $Ne_n=ne_n$ by [F4], and its thermal mean in $\rho_\beta$ equals the absolutely convergent sum $\sum_nnq^n/\sum_nq^n=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)$ with $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$; all higher moments are finite by [F1]. This proves (a). [F1, F4, algebra]

1.3 [The product criterion] Declare the occupation-space effective generator $G$ by $G b_n=\sum_j(\varepsilon_j-\mu)n_j b_n$, including the vacuum with eigenvalue zero; its domain is the set of coefficient families whose squared-energy weighted sum is finite. The occupation bases and [F5] make this a supplied self-adjoint realization of $H-\mu\mathcal N$ as required by the ensemble postulate. In the finite bosonic-partition case all shifted energies are positive, so $G\ge0$. In the finite fermionic-partition case summability implies $\varepsilon_j\to\infty$, hence only finitely many shifted energies are negative, and every fermionic configuration contains each at most once; their finite sum is a lower bound for $G$. Coordinate spectral projections and bounded exponential integration then identify $e^{-\beta G}$ with the diagonal occupation weights. Applying the criterion [F3] to the free-mode energies with chemical-potential shift and combining with the finite products of [F2] gives the stated equivalences for the bosonic and fermionic products, under the stated conditions $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$ (bosons) and no further condition (fermions). This proves (c); normalized weights are the additionally adopted Gibbs preparation, not a derivation of physical equilibration. [F2, F3, F5, algebra]

## Statement

Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], the state postulate P1
and the observable postulate P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the canonical
preparation $\rho_\beta$; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in the
finite-sector class of the entropy definition: the declared model has
finite-dimensional sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$ with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and every declared sector preparation
evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$ under P4 clause (iii). Then:

(a) *entropy is conserved*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$
of the model and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0));$$

(b) *the canonical preparation is stationary*:
$U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$ for every $t$, and every thermal mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ of an assigned observable is time
independent;

(c) *no unitary production of the canonical preparation*: if
$\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ then $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;
equivalently, no evolution of this isolated model maps a non-canonical
declared preparation to the canonical one at any time;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) concern the model's exact unitary flow in the
finite-sector class and the adopted canonical preparation. They assert
nothing about open systems or environment coupling, about the time behaviour
of individual readouts or their time averages, about an approach of any
readout to a thermal value in a limit, about environments or measurement
models, and about any laboratory sample; in particular clause (c) is not a
claim that no physical system ever approaches thermal equilibrium, but the
statement that the model's P4 dynamics alone does not do so.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [Entropy conservation] Let $\rho(0)=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be the spectral decomposition of [F2]. By [F1], $U(t)$ is unitary, so $(U(t)u_i)$ is an orthonormal basis and $\rho(t)=\sum_iw_iT_{U(t)u_i,U(t)u_i}$: the eigenvalues of $\rho(t)$ are the same $w_i$ with the same multiplicities. By [F2] the entropy depends only on that multiset, so $s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0))$ for every $t$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Stationarity of the canonical preparation] By [F3] $\rho_\beta$ is diagonal in the eigenbasis $(v_j)$ of $H_N^\sigma$; the same basis diagonalizes $U(t)$ with eigenvalues $e^{-itE_j/\hbar}$, so $U(t)T_{v_j,v_j}U(t)^*=T_{v_j,v_j}$ for every $j$ and hence $U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$. Every thermal mean $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ is therefore time independent by [F1]. This proves (b). [F1, F3, algebra]

## Example

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with:
one-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$, declared sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ an
orthonormal basis of $K$, particle number $N=1$, single site-occupation
sector, and the declared one-particle operator (the **bond Hamiltonian**)
$$h:=-t\bigl(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle}\bigr),\qquad t>0\ \text{in joules}.$$
Adopt the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and read
$\varepsilon:=2t$ as the tunnelling splitting. Then:

(a) $h$ has the orthonormal eigenbasis
$$u_-:=\frac{|1\rangle+|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad u_+:=\frac{|1\rangle-|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp,$$
so its eigenvalues are $-t$ and $+t$; equivalently $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is the
two-level Hamiltonian of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] with levels $0$ and
$\varepsilon=2t$ and eigenvectors $u_-,u_+$;

(b) the canonical preparation of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ and hence of $h$ is
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}\,T_{u_+,u_+}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},$$
with shifted partition sum $Z_0=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and physical partition trace $Z_h=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}Z_0$;

(c) the exact means, entropy and free energy are
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=\frac{2t}{e^{2\beta t}+1}-t=-t\tanh(\beta t),\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)+\frac{2\beta te^{-2\beta t}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},\qquad F=-\frac1\beta\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)-t,$$
and for every $\beta>0$ one has $-t<\langle h\rangle_\beta<0$ and
$0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$;

(d) *scope*: the computation is an exact statement about the declared
two-dimensional bond model at the assigned temperature; it identifies no
physical double-well or molecular system, asserts no measured splitting and
no transition, and the temperature assignment is the tested identification of
P7.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [Diagonalisation] In the basis $(|1\rangle,|2\rangle)$ the operator $h$ has the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&-t\\-t&0\end{pmatrix}$; the vectors $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ are orthogonal unit vectors and $h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp$ by direct evaluation, so $\{u_-,u_+\}$ is an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues $-t$ and $t$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]. Hence $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ has the eigenvalues $0$ on $u_-$ and $2t$ on $u_+$, and it satisfies the hypothesis of [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$, $u_0=u_-$, $u_1=u_+$. This proves (a). [L1, algebra]

2.1 [Canonical data] Applying [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$ gives $Z=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}T_{u_+,u_+})$ for $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$; since $h=(h+t\,\mathrm{id})-t\,\mathrm{id}$ and both operators are functions of the same eigenbasis, the Gibbs operator of $h$ is the same $\rho_\beta$, because the normalized Gibbs weights are unchanged by the shift: $e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}e^{-\beta(h+tI)}$, so its partition trace is $Z_h=e^{\beta t}Z$ and division gives the same density. The mean of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is $2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)\in(0,t)$, so $\langle h\rangle_\beta=2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)-t=-t\tanh(\beta t)$, which lies in $(-t,0)$ because $e^{2\beta t}>1$ for $\beta t>0$; the entropy formula is that of [L1] at $\varepsilon=2t$ and satisfies $0\le s<\log2$ by [L1], and $F=-\beta^{-1}\log(1+e^{-2\beta t})-t$ is the free energy of $h$ by [L2] and [L1]. This proves (b) and (c) apart from the scope clause. [L1, L2, step 1.1, algebra]

## Example

Adopt P1, P2 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ with $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ in joules.

**Fermionic model.** One-particle space $K=\mathbb C^3$ with modes
$f_1,f_2,f_3$, fermionic statistics $\sigma=-$, $N=2$, and the declared
one-particle operator $h:=\varepsilon\,(0\cdot T_{f_1,f_1}+1\cdot T_{f_2,f_2}+2\cdot T_{f_3,f_3})$.

**Bosonic model.** One-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$ with modes $g_1,g_2$,
bosonic statistics $\sigma=+$, $N=2$, and $h':=\varepsilon(0\cdot T_{g_1,g_1}+1\cdot T_{g_2,g_2})$.

Then:

(a) in the fermionic model the antisymmetric sector has orthonormal
eigenbasis $e_{\{1,2\}}^\wedge,e_{\{1,3\}}^\wedge,e_{\{2,3\}}^\wedge$ with
energies $\varepsilon,2\varepsilon,3\varepsilon$; the partition sum and the
exact occupation means are
$$Z_{\mathrm F}=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon},$$
$$\langle N_1\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},\quad \langle N_2\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},\quad \langle N_3\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},$$
with $\langle N_1+N_2+N_3\rangle_\beta=2$ and ground energy
$\varepsilon$ (configuration $\{1,2\}$);

(b) in the bosonic model the symmetric sector has orthogonal eigenbasis
$m_{(2,0)},m_{(1,1)},m_{(0,2)}$ with energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$;
the partition sum and the exact occupation means are
$$Z_{\mathrm B}=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon},\qquad \langle N_1\rangle_\beta=\frac{2+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm B}},\qquad \langle N_2\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+2e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm B}},$$
with $\langle N_1+N_2\rangle_\beta=2$ and ground energy $0=N\varepsilon_1$;

(c) *scope*: the computations are exact statements about the declared
finite-mode models at the assigned temperature; they assert no physical
species, no measured occupation, no thermalisation and no thermodynamic
limit.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [Fermionic configuration sum] The two-element subsets of $\{1,2,3\}$ are $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$ with energies $0+\varepsilon=\varepsilon$, $0+2\varepsilon=2\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon+2\varepsilon=3\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_J=e^{-\beta\lambda_J}/Z_{\mathrm F}$, and the occupation means are $\sum_Jq_J\mathbf 1_J(j)$ by [L2], giving the three displayed formulas. The total occupation is $\sum_Jq_J\cdot2=2$ because every configuration has two occupied modes, and the smallest energy is that of $\{1,2\}$, namely $\varepsilon$, by [L1] clause (c). This proves (a). [L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 [Bosonic configuration sum] The occupation vectors of total two in two modes are $(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)$ with energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_\lambda=e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}/Z_{\mathrm B}$ and the occupation means are $\sum_\lambda q_\lambda\lambda_j$ by [L2], giving $\langle N_1\rangle=(2\cdot1+1\cdot e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+0)/Z_{\mathrm B}$ and $\langle N_2\rangle=(0+1\cdot e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+2\cdot e^{-2\beta\varepsilon})/Z_{\mathrm B}$, and the total occupation is $2$ because every configuration has $\sum_j\lambda_j=2$; the ground energy is $0=N\varepsilon_1$ by [L1] clause (c). This proves (b). [L1, L2, algebra]

2.1 [Checks and scope] In both models $Z$ is a finite sum of positive terms, hence $0<Z<\infty$; the displayed occupation sums equal the particle number $N=2$ identically in $\beta$ by steps 1.1-1.2, and the ground energies agree with the general formulas of [L1] clause (c) for the sorted energy lists $(0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon)$ and $(0,\varepsilon)$. Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-dimensional model; no physical species, measured occupation, thermalisation or thermodynamic limit entered, which is (c). [L1, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

anchors.claim_quote:
## Example

Adopt the mode models and thermal readings of
[[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ with $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and put $x:=\beta\varepsilon>0$ and
$q:=e^{-x}\in(0,1)$ for a single mode of energy $\varepsilon>0$ (or, in the
grand-canonical reading, $x=\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)$ with $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$).
Then:

(a) the exact single-mode means and their dilute identities are
$$\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm B}=\frac{q}{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \langle N\rangle_{\mathrm F}=\frac{q}{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q},$$
so the bosonic mean exceeds $q$ by $q^2/(1-q)$ and the fermionic mean falls
below $q$ by $q^2/(1+q)$ exactly;

(b) at $q=1/10$ the exact means are $\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm B}=1/9$ and
$\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm F}=1/11$, and the exact identities
$1/9=1/10+1/90$ and $1/11=1/10-1/110$ verify the two remainder formulas;

(c) for the free-mode energies $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$,
$j\ge1$, the sums $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$
converge, so the bosonic and fermionic product partitions are finite
(bosonic case with $\mu<\varepsilon$); for the constant energies
$\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$ the sum $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}=+\infty$
diverges, so both product partitions diverge;

(d) *scope*: the identities and the check are exact statements about the
declared mode models at the assigned temperature and, where stated, chemical
potential; no measured occupation, dilute gas, thermodynamic limit or
condensation is asserted.

step_quotes.quote: 1.3 [The two convergence examples] For $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$ the sum is $\sum_{j\ge1}(e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})<\infty$ by [L2], and for the bosonic product one needs in addition $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j=\varepsilon$; for $\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$ every term of the sum equals $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}>0$, so the sum diverges and [L2] makes both product partitions infinite. This proves (c). [L2, algebra]

anchors.claim_quote:
## Statement

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], work in the
**two-site bond model** of
[[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] with coupling $t>0$,
sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$, bond Hamiltonian
$h=-t(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle})$ and eigenbasis
$u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with $hu_\mp=\mp tu_\mp$, and adopt
the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Consider the hypothetical declared
preparation $\rho(0):=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ (the particle localised at
site $1$) evolving by $\rho(\tau)=U(\tau)\rho(0)U(\tau)^*$ with
$U(\tau)=\exp(-i\tau h/\hbar)$. Then:

(a) $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$, and for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$: the unitary evolution of the model never produces
the canonical preparation from this preparation;

(b) the site-$1$ occupation readout $P_1:=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ has the
exact mean
$$\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=\cos^2\!\Bigl(\frac{t\tau}{\hbar}\Bigr),$$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=1/2$; in particular
$\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1\ne1/2$, so at the initial time the readout does not
take its canonical mean;

(c) the energy readout $h$ has the constant mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\tau)h)=0$ for every $\tau$, while its canonical mean
is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; hence the energy
readout never takes its canonical thermal value;

(d) *scope and interpretation*: the scenario is a hypothetical,
exactly-solved model deduction in one declared preparation; it shows that
agreement or disagreement of individual readout means with their canonical
values is not convergence of the preparation to the canonical one, and that
the model's P4 dynamics does not produce the canonical ensemble. It asserts
no observed equilibration or non-equilibration of a sample, no measured
occupation or energy, and no claim about environments or open systems.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [The evolved preparation and the site readout] With $\psi_0=|1\rangle=(u_-+u_+)/\sqrt2$, [F1] gives $\psi(\tau)=U(\tau)\psi_0=(e^{i\theta}u_-+e^{-i\theta}u_+)/\sqrt2$, where $\theta:=t\tau/\hbar$; by [F2] and $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ this equals $\cos\theta\,|1\rangle+i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, a unit vector. Since $T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}=\tfrac12(I+\sigma_z)$ with $\sigma_z=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}-T_{|2\rangle,|2\rangle}$, and $\sigma_z\psi(\tau)=\cos\theta\,|1\rangle-i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, the site-occupation mean is $\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=|\cos\theta|^2=\cos^2\theta=\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)$, in particular $\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Canonical means and the initial comparison] By [F3], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; moreover $\rho_\beta$ is diagonal in the basis $(u_-,u_+)$ with strictly positive diagonal weights, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta\sigma_z)=0$ because $\sigma_z$ exchanges the two basis vectors, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=\tfrac12$; and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)P_1)=1\ne\tfrac12$, so $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$. [F3, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [The evolved preparation and the site readout] With $\psi_0=|1\rangle=(u_-+u_+)/\sqrt2$, [F1] gives $\psi(\tau)=U(\tau)\psi_0=(e^{i\theta}u_-+e^{-i\theta}u_+)/\sqrt2$, where $\theta:=t\tau/\hbar$; by [F2] and $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ this equals $\cos\theta\,|1\rangle+i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, a unit vector. Since $T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}=\tfrac12(I+\sigma_z)$ with $\sigma_z=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}-T_{|2\rangle,|2\rangle}$, and $\sigma_z\psi(\tau)=\cos\theta\,|1\rangle-i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, the site-occupation mean is $\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=|\cos\theta|^2=\cos^2\theta=\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)$, in particular $\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1$. The scenario uses N=1 and a two-dimensional sector; the readout algebra is two-by-two.
